rationale: Two critical, code-verified defects: router.tsx's isDataSourcesSurfaceEnabled (line 677) is a module-level const evaluated at import time, before appInfoStore.fetchCustomerConfig() ever resolves, so isFeatureEnabled() always sees isConfigFetched=false and dataSourceRoutes is permanently excluded from the route table regardless of the real backend flag values (CR-002); consequently Navigation.tsx crashes with a route-not-found error whenever a flag genuinely enables the surface, because router.resolve({name:'data-sources'}) targets a route id the static table never registers (CR-001). router.test.tsx's passing tests mask this because they set isConfigFetched=true before importing the router module, an ordering the real app never uses. Both lenses and the standards audit ran cleanly with no coverage gap (0 deferred, 0 dismissed); acceptance's AC 'unfiltered when a flag is enabled' is corrected from pass to fail given this evidence.

findings.title: Navigation crashes when Data Sources flag enabled
findings.problem: Navigation.tsx computes isDataSourcesSurfaceEnabled reactively via useFeatureFlag (lines 71-75), and once true, the upperSecondaryItems useMemo (lines 126-131) calls router.resolve({ name: 'data-sources' }). Because router.tsx's static route table never registers the 'data-sources' route id (see CR-002), useVueRouter's findRouteObject throws 'Route with ID "data-sources" was not found.'
findings.impact: Whenever any of the three retrieval flags is genuinely enabled on the backend, Navigation throws during render, crashing the nav bar/app shell for that user instead of surfacing Data Sources — the opposite of the required 'behaves exactly as today' outcome for enabled customers.
findings.recommendation: Fix the router-side gating (CR-002) so the route always exists whenever the flag is live; additionally guard upperSecondaryItems construction so it never resolves a route name absent from the live route table.

findings.title: Data Sources routes permanently excluded from router
findings.problem: isDataSourcesSurfaceEnabled (router.tsx:677-680) is a module-level const evaluated synchronously when router.tsx is imported, calling isFeatureEnabled() (utils/featureFlags.ts:44-51) which returns false whenever appInfoStore.isConfigFetched is false. appInfoStore.fetchCustomerConfig() only runs inside useInitialDataFetch's post-mount useEffect (src/hooks/appLevel/useInitialDataFetch.tsx:29), which fires after router.tsx has already been imported and its module-level routes/router consts (lines 682-722) already built. isConfigFetched is therefore guaranteed false at evaluation time.
findings.impact: dataSourceRoutes is excluded from the route table on every real page load regardless of what the three flags actually resolve to on the backend — confirmed by router.test.tsx passing only because it sets mockAppInfoStore.isConfigFetched = true and calls vi.resetModules() before importing router.tsx, an ordering the real app never uses. This breaks the requirement that Data Sources stay reachable and behave exactly as today when at least one flag is enabled.
findings.recommendation: Gate the route inclusion reactively instead of a frozen module-level boolean — e.g. wrap each dataSourceRoutes entry in the existing FeatureGuard component (as used for other flag-gated routes) so the check re-evaluates against live config instead of a snapshot taken at import time.
